requirement: Fix Happy recovery/session tracking debt and targeted OOM protection, excluding coarse whole-daemon memory limits.

measured.value: Most manually recovered sessions are PPID=1 while daemon snapshot uses pidToTrackedSession only; stable-loss recovery and peak fallback exist in current script.

expected.source: User requirement and specialist findings: restored sessions must be truthful, manual stop/archive must not be resurrected, OOM protection must target runaway sessions.

root_cause_analysis.summary: Recovery script conflates external process spawn with daemon-tracked restore and live watcher treats stable low counts/peak deltas as restore-worthy, overriding user intent. Emergency memory protection needs targeted session action semantics rather than daemon-wide limits.

scope: Make recovery reporting truthful about daemon tracking
Harden emergency guard targeted session protection

acceptance_criteria: Stable low-count live watcher aborts instead of auto-restores
Peak snapshots are not used as runtime desired count
No overclaim that external restored sessions are daemon-tracked
Targeted OOM session action path exists without whole-daemon cap

scope_expansion.reason: Operational script hardening with explicit file scope
